fact: Econet Ai, a subsidiary of Econet Wireless Zimbabwe, runs the Shona-language chatbot Yamurai, which the company says already handles more than 70% of customer enquiries.
Econet Ai is building a Ndebele-speaking chatbot trained on thousands of hours of recorded Ndebele speech, to launch in phases from September 2026.
Techzim reports that Econet AI, launched in April 2026, is working on local language AI, including making its Yamurai assistant sound more Zimbabwean.

The Herald reports the government commissioned a US$350,000 National Information Access Centre at Zimbabwe Open University's Hatcliffe campus, equipped with an Nvidia GPU-powered AI server, opened by Minister Frederick Shava.

The Herald reports the National Information Access Centre at Zimbabwe Open University, Hatcliffe, opened with an Nvidia GPU-powered AI server that Minister Shava says enables practical AI training and advanced analytics.
Minister Mavetera said a 'Penguin AI' project to create local datasets for AI systems would be launched before December 2026.

Data Center Dynamics reports that Seattle-based Chillmine signed an MoU with Energywise to develop solar-powered data centres in Zimbabwe expected to support AI Infrastructure-as-a-Service, with no sites or construction timelines disclosed.
